criteria.text: A business in rural Atlantic Canada (which includes Newfoundland and Labrador)
criteria.quote: Entrepreneurs or businesses purchasing a new or existing company in rural Atlantic Canada;

criteria.text: The business is in a rural area
criteria.quote: Entrepreneurs or businesses purchasing a new or existing company in rural Atlantic Canada;

criteria.text: The business has a legitimate chance of economic viability
criteria.quote: Potential borrowers must show a legitimate chance of economic viability.

criteria.text: Creates or keeps jobs without hurting existing businesses in the area
criteria.quote: Employment creation and/or maintenance without negatively impacting existing area businesses is also a necessity.

research.notes: Uses on the page: buying, starting or expanding a business, working capital, land and buildings, equipment and more; they don't map to a purpose rule without leaving some out, so no purpose rule. "Rural" can't be settled from a community answer (the Newcomer page sends St. John's and Mount Pearl to Metro Business Opportunities, but no list of rural places is given), so it is check-this-yourself. The page says CBDCs can exceed $150,000 in certain circumstances. Intake: not stated. Contacts: the offices of CBDC Central (Grand Falls-Windsor), CBDC Gander Area and CBDC Emerald (Baie Verte, with a Springdale satellite office), each quoted from its own cbdc.ca office page saved as a source of this record; all three pages list this loan. Only the Gander Area page names the places it serves (a list of place names, not census divisions), so census_divisions is null for every office and there is no location rule beyond the province (contract question B). Other CBDCs in the province are not listed as contacts. Office labels name the office and its town only, every word of which is in the contact's own quote (DECISIONS #25); the app's line above several contacts tells an owner to call the office nearest them.
